question: Do decoys only work on creatures that can explain their choices?
answer: No. Female túngara frogs offered two recorded male calls preferred caller B over caller A; when Lea and Ryan added a third, inferior call, the females switched to A. Mate-choice theory had assumed stable rankings, just as rational-choice economics does. The decoy works on a brain that has never heard of a price.
move: When a frog shares your mistake, look for wiring, not motives.
reference: Lea & Ryan, Irrationality in mate choice revealed by túngara frogs, Science, 2015
